Jaddari (F46) / Jadd Empire (F51) Campaign Chain

Survey region: Bulwar.

Starting country: Jaddari (F46) Formable country: Jadd Empire (F51)

One-sentence conclusion: This is an exceptionally long campaign that grows from a desert religious legion into a pan-continental universalist empire: the early game rolls forward on zeal, cavalry and continuous war, while the formed empire turns toward conversion, multi-ethnic administration and a mobile court. Its main pressures are governing capacity, aggressive expansion and an avoidable but extremely dangerous Deioderan civil war.

Story: very high｜Mission-tree length: exceptionally long (21 groups, 120 direct missions)｜Mission-tree update: checked against local v1.37.5.0｜Distinctiveness: very high｜Grind: high｜Early pressure: high｜Expansion capacity: extremely high

Identity and History

Jaddari (F46) is a starting country in 1444; the Jadd Empire (F51) is the formable country in the same campaign chain. After formation, the script continues to unlock the original missions through the “was F46” identity, so this is not an unrelated second country.【Local script】【Local localisation】

At the start, the country uses the Desert Legion reform, has Desert Elf as its primary culture, follows the Jadd, and accepts the Mašnsih and Siadunan Harpy cultures. Its ruler, Jaddar Jexiszuir, is both a missionary and a powerful general, while the legion also begins with high army tradition and professionalism.【Local history script】

The English official Wiki traces the legion's origin to Jaddar's merger of two older legions in 1247 and places the birth of the Jadd here around 1333; the legion then achieved military successes in the Salahad, Bulwar and Rahen before being reorganised into the Jadd Empire.【Wiki material】 These dates supplement the setting only and do not override the current script.

National Story and Campaign Arc

The core of Jaddari is not to build an ordinary Elven kingdom, but to prove that the Jadd can transcend race and region. The first half expands the expeditionary community through war, conversion, Harpy relations and subject relationships such as Velkalgulan; the second half must turn the religious ideal into an imperial system capable of governing several continents.【Local flavour text】

Forming the Jadd Empire requires following the Jadd, being at peace, owning 150 provinces across a broad area of Bulwar or Rahen, and holding seven specified core provinces. On completion, the country becomes an empire, gains a centralisation transition modifier and replaces its missions; the campaign shifts from a mobile legion to capacity, conversion and multi-regional administration.【Local script】

The mission tree spans Bulwar, the Salahad, Rahen, Haless and Cannor. Its continuity comes from the progression “expeditionary legion—religious state—multi-ethnic empire—identity crisis”, rather than from a mere pile of territorial requirements.

Core Mechanics

Jaddari zeal. War, victories and conversion sustain zeal, while peace and unconverted territory consume it. The player can spend zeal on legion leaders, a ten-year military bonus or rapid cavalry reinforcement. The current script determines the numbers; Dev Diary 69 explains the design purpose of replacing generic tribal loyalty with this system.【Local script】【Official dev diary】

Institutionalising the faith. The Lightbringer order, great temples, regional conversion and the requirements for guardians of the faith turn conquest into permanent religious nodes and state institutions. They continually compete for administrative points, diplomatic points, money and peace windows, so the campaign cannot be played only to a military rhythm.【Local script】

Mobile court and east–west orientation. After forming F51, the court can move between eligible core provinces. Moving the capital, remaining in place and developing regions change the empire's east–west orientation and affect the direction of the later crisis; this is a governing trade-off, not a free capital move.【Local script】

Deioderan. When cross-continental development and east–west orientation reach the relevant conditions, the empire may split into eastern and western halves and enter civil war, while suffering penalties to unrest, war exhaustion, manpower recovery and administrative efficiency. The crisis can be avoided through route control; if it occurs, the player can reunify diplomatically, reunify by war or accept a lasting partition.【Local script】

Phased Play

Early game: Use high tradition, professionalism and cavalry strength to establish yourself quickly in Bulwar while managing zeal. War keeps the legion's tempo, but conquered land must be converted promptly or peace will rapidly drain your resources.

Preparing formation: Plan wars around the 150 provinces and seven core provinces. Do not wait until the territory is complete before preparing administrative points, stability and peace windows. Subjects can share the burden of occupation and capacity, but the formation conditions and religious unity still have to be handled.

Imperial phase: After forming F51, reassess capacity, autonomy, religious nodes and court location. The mobility advantage of the legion period remains, but the imperial missions place greater emphasis on broad administration; mobile-court choices also accumulate the later orientation.

Late game: Decide in advance whether to allow Deioderan. To avoid civil war, control east–west development and orientation; to experience the full crisis, reserve manpower, stability, diplomatic points and a reliable army for the reunification war after the split.

Formable Country and Endgame

Jadd Empire ideas turn legion combat power into long-term expansion capacity, with an emphasis on administrative efficiency, governing capacity, manpower from true-faith provinces, discipline, movement speed and warscore cost against other religions. Formation also applies a transitional modifier that strengthens the army while reducing tax, production, naval and capacity values; it must not be described as a pure bonus.【Local script】

The endgame goal is to maintain a Jadd Empire across several continents through religious nodes, regional capitals and ethnic integration. The final stretch also requires a powerful mage ruler and the third level of Enchantment, so magic is not the everyday core loop but can become a hard gate for the final missions.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

The local future plan lists the “non-Jaddari route to the Jadd Empire” as paused; it is separate from the F46→F51 route in this article and must not be treated as unfinished late-game content for the current campaign.【Document record】

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 95/100｜Autocracy 85/100｜Magic↔Artifice 70/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 20/100)｜Pluralism 70/100.

The v2.1 value score is Good (74/100), with a stable trajectory. A cross-racial universalist community, ethnic inclusion and institution-building provide clear positive evidence; continuous holy war and forced conversion mainly reduce restraint and pluralism, while conquest and imperialisation are not deducted again on their own.

Recommended for players who enjoy exceptionally long mission trees, cavalry and mobile warfare, religious expansion, multi-ethnic empires and high-risk civil wars. Not recommended for players who prefer peaceful development, overseas colonisation, short campaigns or avoiding long-term governing-capacity management.

Community Experience

【Community opinion】A recent 2026 guide considers the revised route more controllable than the old one, but still identifies early expansion, aggressive expansion and capacity as the main pressures; its discussion of submods and different racial armies is not a single optimal route.

【Community opinion】A 2025 Deioderan experience post records army defections and differences between eastern and western development. It does not identify an exact version, so it only establishes that players encountered these runtime shocks and cannot stand in for the current disaster script.

Evidence Boundary

This article concerns the local base mod and localisation at v1.37.5.0, checked on 16 September 2026. Identity, formation, mission ownership, legion zeal, religious decisions, the mobile court and the Deioderan core come from current local scripts; the official Wiki and dev diaries provide historical and design context only.

The local offline Wiki was checked for Jaddari Legion (page_id=947, revision_id=32622), Jadd Empire (2618/32623) and The Jadd (1320/32223). The 1562 founding date and decline after Deioderan belong to the official setting timeline, not an inevitable player-campaign outcome; the Jadd page is still marked as being written and was not used to fill in a complete religious history.

Reddit research found three directly related official materials; the 18.5 update is explicitly an April Fools temporary branch and is not part of the formal canon. Two player posts are retained separately. The Great Holy War CB, some event tails and the exact unlock dates of special units remain unresolved, but this does not change the article's conclusions about the country's history and core play.

For complete sources, paths and conflict notes, see the evidence record.

National ideas (reference appendix)

Native English national-idea names and descriptions are reproduced below with the inherited effect displays. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Alternative sets and successor ideas do not automatically stack. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals, not events already completed in 1444. Native English wording is reused rather than back-translating embellished Chinese localisation. Inherited display-unit assumptions remain unverified; this translation does not correct source data.

Jaddari (F46) — Jaddari Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
            tag = F46 #Jaddari
    }

Traditions: Jaddari Traditions

Effects: Army attrition: -20%; Discipline: +5%.

Idea 1: Jaddari Tolerance

Jaddar realised that the Bulwari Sun Cultists were misguided in their understanding of Surael. The failure of Jaher to do his duty meant that the mission could not rest with a single individual or race, but all races should be incorporated in the duties of Surael. No people should be excluded, so long as they do their part.

Effects: Promote culture cost: -25%; Number of accepted cultures: +1.

Idea 2: Desert Phoenix

When Jaher's Phoenix Legions returned to Bulwar many of them found a new and strange land that they could not find their home in. They returned to the desert and carved out a new life for themselves in this desolate land. Adapting their battle experience to the wide desert plains, the Phoenix Legions transformed into the mounted Desert Phoenixes.

Effects: Land leader maneuver: +1; Cavalry combat ability: +25%.

Idea 3: The Golden Highway

Under Jaher's rule, the Phoenix Empire constructed a great road connecting Bulwar to Haless. Over it many goods and troops flowed east and west. This primary artery goes through the heart of our land and we are its guardian. While the road itself may have fallen into disrepair, the route is still there and we control its traffic.

Effects: Caravan power: +20%.

Idea 4: The Heir of Jexis

Jexis, daughter of Jaher, reforged the Phoenix Empire before being assassinated. Unknown to many, she had a son, Jaddar, who is the founder of our nation. While some may disagree about his true heritage, it is clear that we who forged the Phoenix Empire are the true successors of the dynasty.

Effects: Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Horde unity: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3.

Idea 5: Independent Missions

Our tolerance of all within the Jadd puts the duties to all within the Jadd. Their duties include that of making others see the light. This responsibility on an individual level takes away some of the burden of spreading the light from the government, allowing for a less hands on approach to the integration of new peoples.

Effects: Missionary maintenance cost: -33%.

Idea 6: Banish the Dark

It is our duty to Surael to banish the dark and spread the light. There are many in the world who do not see this the right way, we shall bring them the truth. If not through word, through fire and blood.

Effects: War score cost against other religions: -20%.

Idea 7: Armies of the Faithful

The followers of the Jadd are full of righteous zeal. We have stimulated their martial zest and now the faithful flock to our banners. The armies of the Jadd will be great and numerous.

Effects: Manpower recovery speed: +20%.

Ambition: Jaddari Ambition

Effects: Army tradition: +1.

Jadd Empire (F51) — Jadd Empire Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
        OR = {
            tag = F51 #Jadd Empire
            tag = F99 #Jadd Empire Civil War
        }
    }

Traditions: Jadd Empire Traditions

Effects: Cavalry combat ability: +20%; Missionary strength: +2%.

Idea 1: Expand the Legions

When the Legions adopted the Jadd, they also opened up their ranks to a much greater variety of people and races. While this was initially disruptive and led to a decrease in discipline and organization, it also had as an immediate effect that it greatly increased the manpower pool the state could draw from. This allowed the Jadd Empire to pull on greater amounts of men than their neighbours.

Effects: Manpower from true faith provinces: +20%.

Idea 2: Native Bureaucrats

All within the Jadd are equal and it would not do to suppress any cultures or races. So the Jadd Empire followed a practice of leaving local administrations intact to cause minimal disruption. Where feudal systems existed, the local lords needed to report to the imperial governor, but the rest was left intact. The same occurred with more modern administrations. Only in very tribal systems with no clear power structure was order brought by restructuring the local systems, but local chiefs still stayed in power. Of course all of this was if they did not revolt. This system allowed large areas to be swiftly integrated and reduced the need for forming new local administrations.

Effects: Governing Capacity Modifier: +20%.

Idea 3: Spread the Faith

At the heart of the Jadd Empire stood the faith of the Jadd. While proclaiming the empire had given the faith a clear home and base to rally around, the Jadd was not an isolationist religion. Its core tenet was the banishment of the dark, so the Empire ever sought to expand its borders and to spread the faith to new lands. It could not rest until the darkness was banished from all lands.

Effects: War score cost against other religions: -20%.

Idea 4: Restructure the Legions

The old Phoenix Legions underwent great changes since the Sun Elves first landed on shores of Bulwar. The experience they gained while campaigning through Sarhal and Haless made them strong. The adaptation to the eastern Salahad made them crafty. The next reform would leave them changed to an even greater degree. The mixing of different races into the army would have made them unrecognisable to Jaher's army. However the experience and drill of their veterans forged these different groups into one force, now also driven by a common purpose: To defend and to spread the Light of the Jadd.

Effects: Discipline: +5%.

Idea 5: Rebuild the Golden Highway

The Golden Highway of Jaher was the greatest infrastructure project the world had seen until that point. So great that the following generations could not keep up with its maintenance. Until the Jadd Empire stepped in and reconnected the ancient Bulwari lands with its core lands around the Mountain of Clear Sight. A new highway was constructed in the place of the old one, recreating the connection between Haless and Bulwar. Its control gave the Jadd greater power over its trade and also allowed swift movement of troops from one end of the empire to another.

Effects: Trade efficiency: +10%; Movement speed: +15%.

Idea 6: Increase Lightbringer Jurisdiction

The order of Lightbringers was a class of warriors, scribes, rhetoricians and clerics that had as a task to safeguard the light within the state. Their tasks mainly revolved around seeking out heathens and heretics and either making them see the light, or bringing them to trial. In the days of the Jadd Empire their powers were extended to bypass the courts and to instantly deal with anyone who did not comply with the tenets of the faith. This would lead to occasional riots and more than one instance of the burning of innocents, but it did quicken the spread of the faith within the Empire.

Effects: True faith tolerance: +1; Harsh treatment cost: -25%.

Idea 7: The True Successors of Surael

Since time immemorial the central question of the Bulwari religion has been how the world responds to the death or return of Surael. The Sun Cult proclaimed Jaher to be the god's reincarnation, and when he died the Sun Elves were appointed as the successors. Jaddar claimed that all people who follow the truth would be Surael's successors. In turn those who follow the Jadd see their leader as the Divine Herald and the voice of the Sun God.

Effects: Army morale: +10%; Yearly absolutism: +1.

Ambition: Jadd Empire Ambition

Effects: Administrative efficiency: +5%.
